elements.text: Flight crew's failure to maintain adequate airspeed
Aerodynamic stall from which the crew did not recover
Flight crew failed to maintain appropriate course and speed for the approach
Flight crew failed to properly configure the airplane at the start of the approach
Flight crew failed to monitor the airplane’s airspeed during later stages of the approach
Flight crew allowed airspeed to decrease to a dangerously low level
Flight crew failed to recognize that a stall was imminent
Flight crew failed to execute a go-around despite inadequate airspeed or CDI deflection
Flight crew not adhering to Aviation Charter’s approach procedures
Flight crew not effectively applying crew resource management techniques
Pilots had previously demonstrated potentially serious performance deficiencies consistent with below-average flight proficiency
Aviation Charter not operating in accordance with weight and balance load manifest procedures
Aviation Charter did not have adequate stall recovery guidance
Aviation Charter did not have consistent deicer boot operational guidance
Aviation Charter did not have an in-range checklist
Aviation Charter not adequately making company pilots aware of its Standard Operating Procedures
Aviation Charter not training pilots on CRM in accordance with its FAA-approved module
FAA surveillance was not sufficient to detect discrepancies at Aviation Charter
Flight crewmembers were properly certificated and trained
No evidence of preexisting medical or physical conditions affecting crew performance
Fatigue most likely did not degrade pilot performance
Accident airplane was properly certificated, equipped, and maintained
No evidence of preexisting powerplant, system, or structural failures
Weight and balance were within limits
Clouds might have prevented seeing the airport
Icing did not affect airplane performance
Controller instructions did not prevent safe interception of approach course
VOR signal issues were not a factor
Recommendation: En route inspections and ground training are essential for oversight
Recommendation: Extend CRM training to all Part 135 dual-pilot operations
Recommendation: Install low-airspeed alert systems
